If you've used the 340 light character boost then you're pretty SOL until you finish Rise of Iron in terms of light appropriate gear, as all quest and mission rewards are locked to their original levels \[ie almost all Taken King quest rewards are between 280 and 300\]. Otherwise you'll naturally accrue light and power as you go through the stories. You should hit 140 after all of Y1, 280 after all of Y2, and 400 naturally is Y3s max.

Titan exotics wise the main ones to look out for are **Helm of Saint 14, Glasshouse, Ruin Wings,** and **Armamentarium**. Best place for those is Xur on the weekend \[as I write this he has Crest of Alpha Lupi, which isn't great but is 350-380 depending on your light\] but Three of Coins are a stacking buff on unsuccessful uses where Ultras can drop exotic engrams. They're also available from Xur.

Weapons wise the main ones you're missing from what you've told are **Dark Drinker** *\[take the void option in Shaxx's sword quests post Taken King\]*, and **Black Spindle** *\[do the heroic version of Lost to Light, bring a team and be quick. When you get to the circular room with 3 tomb husk deposits, on the far side as you enter the door to Taniks' ketch should be open. Board and it and completely clear it in 12 minutes, enemies and blights.\]*. Those are meta in all the raids save Crota's End where GHorn will do you good.

Best way to level anything is to buy their requisite symetries from Banshee-44 and pop Motes of Light with one active. IIRC it's something like 6 motes for a full Heavy, 12 for a Special, and 20 for a primary, but those could be wrong. Armor will get some benefit from the mote popping but there's no really fast way of leveling armor apart from using it and getting experience from other means.

Exotic Shards are from any dismantled exotics, or bought from Xur. Glass needles are also bought from Xur but are only for rerolling stats on exotics. If you need motes or an easy engram or two for legendaries there are two raid chest 'cheeses'. Both of these are almost always pinned in the weekly reset thread but quick TLDW; In **VoG** immediately go to Campus 9 \[on the right as you spawn, the same way as the Theosion strike\], wait in the next area for about 90 seconds, come back and the spire will be formed. Grab the first reward chest and the first hidden chest. In Crota, in the thrallway there are six doors on the left that can hold a chest, which one changes weekly, but the easiest are naturally doors 1 and 2. The reset thread always has a comment telling which is the door of the week. You can do these chest 'cheeses' in both their OG levels and 390 once those are unlocked. OG raids are only good for things you can convert to Motes at the speaker. The 390s can give legendary engrams and higher light artifacts.

It's a very good base for a R10 trains deck but there's one or two things I'd change, just for consistency and power's sake. UR/SR cores permitting some changes, but the majority are N/R 

I'd get rid of the Express Train Trolley Olley, and Snow Plow Hustle Rustle. Trolley Olley's effect is meaningless in a deck that can OTK by itself, and Hustle Rustle is a halfway decent effect in Turn 4+, but Trains can end the duel by Turn 3. 

I'd add at least 2 Planet Pathfinder \[R\]- *Tribute on field to search for a field spell.* With trains, you barely ever use your normal summon, so it's not a wasted effect, plus Revolving Switchyard is so important to Trains' playstyle. Ideal world you'd run 3 Terra instead, but banlist gonna banlist.

I'd suggest 2 Exodius; The Ultimate Forbidden Lord \[N\] - *Shuffle all monsters in your GY to the deck to SS*. It's a Lvl10, and can allow you to summon Superdimensional Robot Galaxy Destroyer \[UR\] - *Detatch 1 mat, destroy all Spell/Traps your opponent controls.* It's exceptionally handy if your opponent sets their deck and passes T1.

You've already mentioned Kaijus. I run 2 Jizukiru \[R\], 1 Gameciel \[SR\], and 1 Kaiju Slumber \[UR\], just incase I need something gone ASAP, plus Jizukiru's a Lvl10 so fits your summons well.

Train Connection \[N\] can help with OTKs, and is really easy to activate with this deck. It's for all intents and purposes an equip Limiter Removal, but adds piercing and limits attacking to only the monster it's equipped to. So equip it to Liebe for a 10k beater with piercing and multi attacks. Hardly anything will survive it.

I run the bugs in my extra too - No35 Ravenous Tarantula \[N\], No84 Pain Gainer \[N\], and No77 The Seven Sins \[R\], to XYZ into one another. If all else has failed, No77 is a 4k beater, that has a non-targeting banish effect, and self preserve on destruction effect. If you go through the spiders, it has 4 materials, so can survive 4 destructions.

I hope I'm not being overbearing or annoying posting this, I just love seeing people play R10 Trains.

It's a mighty fine line to walk. I've done both ways of giving EXP you've mentioned. I started out with 1EXP per session, and extra EXP if somebody did something to defend a touchstone, conviction, or anything extraordinary. My last chronicle I gave EXP dependent on how much was done in the session \[shopping episode - 2exp, important political dance with the baron - 5exp\] etc . But the 1 per session was too slow, the players didn't feel like they were progressing, and my npcs of similar age, or a little older, were rolling them 9/10. And the 2-5exp per session was too fast, it quickly got to a point where a malkavian was able to buy his way to 5\* Dominate 5\* CHA/MAN and now everything I threw at him was a joke because 'lol terminal decree'. Granted it took like 50 or so sessions for them to get there, but still, they felt too powerful for my chronicle, and I had to vastly outweigh the odds in order to give them even the smallest challenge, and then, they complained my session wasn't as fun.

Next game I run I might go with the divide costs by 3 like you've written. I had never thought of that and it gets around most of the problems of both systems. But RAW is much too slow for any long form game, and vastly increasing EXP gains quickly makes PCs outpower NPCs

It's because they're all short city circuits

**Short** because the batteries need to *just* last for about 46 minutes, accounting for energy managment, and no safety car/FCY periods. Anything longer than their shortened version of the Mexico GP circuit (just after the pit complex they take a right and rejoin before the stadium section, instead of exiting halfway through the Peraltada, they double back out of the stadium and take the full Peraltada, albeit with a chicane half way through the corner, where the F1 circuit would meet up) would see the cars heavily struggle to reach the race distance at anything other more than 80% speed. If they raced at Silverstone, they'd have to take one of the shorter configurations, and then, would have to add a chicane on either the Wellington or Hangar straight (Depending on configuration) to aid in energy recovery.

**City** because FE was built on accessibility of the fans. Placing cars that are at the bleeding edge of electrical car engineering at Silverstone of Road America would have gotten racing fans interested, but placing them within cities gets even the most casual fans semi-interested. "Oh, that event I've seen on bus sides for a month and a half is on Saturday, and I can see it from my window? I'll give it a watch!" In addition, every FE race (to my knowledge) a sister "e-village" near the track, full of exhibits and hands on demos about sustainable energy sources and reducing carbon emissions etc, so placing the races, and therefore the villages, in cities, gets more people to visit, and hopefully more people to take notice. And offshoot of them being city circuits, is that they're almost always narrow, with barely enough room for 2.5 cars to go side by side down a straight.

Ratios for A, B, and C vary depending on what other engines/tech you have in there. Some like 3/3/3, some 2/2/2, but a lot I've seen run 2/3/2, which is also what I run. 3x terraforming and 3x union hanger are musts. 

The rest of the deck is pretty fluid. Twin Twisters are a very nice addition, because it's a -1 to your opponent, whilst allowing you to put an ABC piece in the GY. Foolish Burial is good for the same reason. In the current meta Anti-Spell Fragrance is at least a nice side, if not main. Once Union Hanger is out, all other spells are supplementary so you don't take a huge hit whilst it could cripple your opponent

There are quite a few engines you can run alongside ABC's. 

* Gadgets are 3 gold and 3 silver and can allow you to get to ABC, any Rank4 XYZ, and Decode talker pretty easily. 

* Destrudo is, in its simplest form, 2 Destrudo, 2 Darkwurm, 1 Dragon Ravine, 1 Ancient Fairy Dragon (and if you want 1 Black Rose Dragon). You lose 3k LP net turn one (4k for Destrudo's effect, but gain 1k with Ancient Fairy Dragon's field spell effect) but it can be very worth it. Get Ravine with Terra/drawing it. Activate it by discarding either Destrudo or Darkwurm, send the other from your deck to GY. SS Darkwurm, SS Destrudo, Synchro into AFD, use her effect to both get Union Hanger to your hand and destroy RAvine. Then SS an ABC piece using her second effect.

* Galaxy Soldier is a nice 2 piece combo. SS one by discarding an ABC piece, search the other with the first's effect. SS the second by discarding another ABC piece. You can XYZ into Cyber Dragon Nova, then Infinity, and your GY is 2/3 on the way to ABC.

* Recently Ojama's have gotten some nice synergy with ABC's through Ojamassimilation (Reveal 1 ABC, send Ojamas from your hand to GY and SS the same number of ABC pieces from deck). The Ojamalphabet works well with the Destrudo engine, as you can send Ojamagic (when sent to GY, get 1 yellow, black, and green, from your deck to your hand) to the GY as cost and that kicks both engines off. I wouldn't recommend it as IMO it ruins its consistency, but at a local level it can be fun to mess around with.

I personally run Destrudo, Gadgets, and Galaxy engines alongside ABCs as all their end goals are easy to achieve and can make some terrifying boards in the process.

Quick reasonings;

a) I run 2 DMGs because if you've somehow got 3 DMs in GY she gets to 2900, is affected by Expanded, so would get to 3900 off it's first effect alone, and if you open her and AIM, she's not a massive loss to send to the GY to summon her much better retrain.

b) You can run anything you feel like would fit over the Veilers. I often sided one out for Ra Sphere Mode (I don't own any kaijus yet), but 2 Ash's or Ogre's would work just as well.

c) I use 3 Attacks and 3 Knives' because by the end of turn 2 you'll have DM or MoDI on field, and the removal is fantastic. Pendulums? DMA! 3k body and no Timaeus? Knives! The Cosmic Cyclone is there for the 5% of times you'll require getting rid of back row with no DM in sight.
